artists.name: Zhang Kechun
artists.why_relevant: Documents Yellow River regions with similar muted palette, architectural emptiness, and Chinese vernacular subjects. Complementary medium (photography vs painting) creates dialogue rather than competition.

artists.name: Sungseok Ahn
artists.why_relevant: Korean painter depicting urban landscapes with comparable light treatment and architectural focus. Shares nostalgic approach to disappearing cityscapes.

artists.name: Honggoo Kang
artists.why_relevant: Hyperrealist Korean urban scenes with similar nostalgic distance. Different technique (hyperrealism vs atmospheric realism) but shared subject matter and emotional tone.

artists.name: Attasit Pokpong
artists.why_relevant: Thai artist painting Bangkok shophouses and vernacular spaces with parallel preservation impulse. Expands geographic range while maintaining thematic consistency.

artists.name: Chen Qi
artists.why_relevant: Chinese artist working with watercolor on architectural and landscape subjects. More abstract but compatible tonally, shares medium and quiet observation approach.

artists.name: Cai Zebin
artists.why_relevant: Contemporary Chinese realist depicting urban renewal and disappearing neighborhoods. Directly aligned subject matter with documentary-nostalgic approach.

artists.name: Gao Yuan
artists.why_relevant: Documents Chinese alleyways and courtyard life with similar anthropological-nostalgic lens. Photography complements painting, shared cultural and spatial focus.

artists.name: Kazuhiro Hori
artists.why_relevant: Japanese everyday observation painter with overlap in quiet domestic subjects, gouache/watercolor technique, and decorative appeal. Shared aesthetic restraint and medium.

artists.name: He Duoling
artists.why_relevant: Influential Chinese realist painting domestic interiors, part of Sichuan realist lineage. Shares quiet domesticity and likely collector base.

artists.name: Liu Xiaodong
artists.why_relevant: Documentary realism with empathy but without intervention. Observational mode aligns with target artist's detached contemplative approach.

artists.name: Rinko Kawauchi
artists.why_relevant: Photographer capturing gentle observation, domestic scale, light-focused non-narrative moments. Shares emotional tone and subject scale despite different medium.

artists.name: Gideon Rubin
artists.why_relevant: Faceless figures creating anonymity and universality, memory-distance, non-confrontational human presence. Shares emotional restraint and approach to depicting people.

connections.reason: Photography and painting of same cultural subjects creates dialogue. Both document disappearing Chinese vernacular with atmospheric restraint.
Nearly identical subject matter and cultural context. Both contemporary Chinese realists focused on neighborhoods threatened by development.
Shared medium, scale, and approach to everyday life subjects. Compatible collector base interested in accessible realism.
He Duoling as established figure in Chinese realist tradition that target artist extends. Shared collector demographics.
Different media but nearly identical emotional tone and approach to capturing everyday moments through light and atmosphere.
Parallel practices in different Asian countries, both documenting threatened vernacular architecture with preservation mindset.
Shared documentary methodology and non-interventionist observation style in Chinese contemporary painting context.
Both use restraint in depicting human presence to create emotional distance and universal accessibility.

group_show_ideas.title: Thresholds: Domestic Boundaries in Transition
group_show_ideas.concept: Doorways, windows, courtyards as psychological and social spaces. Focus on liminal architecture across Asian contexts.

group_show_ideas.title: Afternoon Light: Temporal Painting in Contemporary Practice
group_show_ideas.concept: Artists obsessed with specific lighting conditions and time-capture. Technical exhibition focusing on how light describes space and emotion.

group_show_ideas.title: The Last Alley: Urban Vernacular Before Erasure
group_show_ideas.concept: Documentary impulse across media examining disappearing neighborhood typologies in developing Asia.

group_show_ideas.title: Inhabited Objects: Still Life as Social Document
group_show_ideas.concept: Potted plants, thermoses, stools as carriers of human presence and class markers. Objects as stand-ins for people and social histories.

group_show_ideas.title: Slow Cities: Counter-Narratives to Asian Hyperdevelopment
group_show_ideas.concept: Work depicting or advocating for preservation, slowness, human scale against megacity narratives and rapid urbanization.

group_show_ideas.title: Empty Rooms, Full Memory: Domestic Interiors as Portraiture
group_show_ideas.concept: Spaces standing in for absent people; rooms as psychological portraits revealing lives through architectural and object traces.

group_show_ideas.title: The Color of Dust: Materiality and Decay in Contemporary Realism
group_show_ideas.concept: Technical exhibition focusing on rendering aged surfaces, patina, weathering. Craft-focused show about depicting time's marks on materials.

shared_themes: light and shadow as primary subject
